interface.name: THICKNESS_FAULT
interface.description: Thickness deviation exceeds the permitted tolerance.

interface.name: THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID
interface.description: Thickness-signal validity; FALSE means the signal is lost or unavailable.

interface.name: FaultTimestamp
interface.description: Current timestamp in seconds, used as the fault-record identifier.

interface.name: CycleTime
interface.description: Actual elapsed interval represented by this invocation; must be positive.

interface.name: THICKNESS_ALARM
interface.description: Thickness alarm with a minimum 500 ms hold duration.

interface.name: Slab_Fault_History
interface.description: Five most recent fault timestamps; index 0 is newest; read-only to callers.

scan_semantics: Inputs I[k] are sampled at invocation; outputs O[k] are observed after the call. Retained pre-state q[k] becomes q[k+1]. Each test resets the instance. A transition affects the same observed scan. dt_ms is elapsed time since the preceding invocation; the first invocation starts IEC timers at elapsed zero. CycleTime inputs, where supplied, are attributed to the current invocation rather than inferred from dt_ms.
safety_priority: Invalid signal overrides minimum alarm holding.
A persistent valid fault keeps the alarm on.
assumptions: The counted signal is valid AND fault; a valid fault after signal loss is a new occurrence.
Hold starts at elapsed zero on the trigger call and releases at 500ms if the fault is absent. A fresh rising trigger restarts the hold.
Invalid input cancels the hold immediately.
Positive CycleTime is added on every current qualifying call, including a normal first invocation.
UINT/LTIME overflow is outside these bounded cases and requires a separate policy.

formal_properties.name: Fault hold
formal_properties.explanation: The alarm persists during fault and hold.

formal_properties.name: Occurrence
formal_properties.explanation: Each valid rising fault shifts the bounded history.

formal_properties.name: No spurious record
formal_properties.explanation: Held faults and invalid inputs do not create records.

formal_properties.name: Runtime
formal_properties.explanation: Normal runtime counts only eligible intervals.

formal_properties.name: Release
formal_properties.explanation: Alarm releases when neither fault nor hold remains.

atomic_propositions.rise: valid AND fault AND NOT previous(valid AND fault)
atomic_propositions.same_stats: count and history equal pre-scan values
atomic_propositions.hold: trigger age<500ms with no intervening signal loss
atomic_propositions.normal: valid AND NOT fault AND CUTTING_RUN
